children: Sandisk (SNDK, Financials) recorded the largest earnings-per-share surprise among technology companies in a Seeking Alpha quantitative screen as the third-quarter earnings season approached its conclusion.

The memory and storage giant topped analysts' consensus earnings projection by $3.10 a share, putting it ahead of other technology companies benefitting from sustained investment in computer infrastructure.

Salesforce came in second with a $2.63 EPS surprise and American Bitcoin was third with a $2.34 surprise. Dell Technologies was fourth with a $2.12 surprise and Micron Technology rounded out the top five with $1.60.

Other businesses beating estimates were Arrow Electronics at $1.26, InterDigital at $1.24 and Sanmina at $1.16. Ubiquiti and SharonAI Holdings completed the top 10 with shocks of $1.07 and $1.03, respectively.
The list includes memory, corporate software and computer hardware and digital infrastructure, a reflection of better-than-expected profitability in a host of technological sectors.

Investment in artificial intelligence continues to be a major industrial driver. Gartner's August projection projects global semiconductor sales to reach over $1.56 trillion in 2026, increasing 92% from 2025.
An EPS surprise is the difference between reported profits per share and the average forecast of analysts.
Investors will be eyeing next earnings projections and AI infrastructure expenditure patterns to assess if these profit beats are a sign of continued growth.

title: Sandisk Leads Tech Stocks in Earnings Surprises Ahead of 8-for-1 Split
